stories.headline: AFL trade and free agency grades - Every club's report card from the 2026 transfer period
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is over. Some teams improved, some stagnated, and others, well, got worse. Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL trade and free agency period is complete. Some teams improved, some have stagnated, and others, well, seemed to have gotten worse.

READ: Every player move from the 2026 off-season

Here's how every team fared over the last two weeks:

Adelaide
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Jordon Butts, Luke Pedlar

2026 draft selections: 15, 32, 35, 43, 56, 92

I'm not sure what the Crows' gameplan was this trade and free agency period, but it's fair to say the club sat on its hands and did next to nothing. Losing key defender Jordon Butts to the Bulldogs obviously weakens them, while just one draft selection inside the top 30 is unlikely to provide much immediate support. Adelaide's list profile remains fine, and maybe they will surprise us all in 2027, but you just get the sense so many other clubs have passed them by over the last two weeks.

Grade: F

Brisbane
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Lachie Neale, Sam Marshall, Will McLachlan, Keidean Coleman

2026 draft selections: 21, 27, 28, 45, 79, 97

The Lions were the biggest winners of last year's off-season (and season!), but this year was a different story. All year it seemed a formality they would lose the services of dual Brownlow Medal winner Lachie Neale, who ultimately signed with Collingwood as a free agent. They also waved goodbye to Keidean Coleman and Sam Marshall, two players who had struggled to crack the best 23 of late. No picks inside the top 20 would be concerning for 17 other clubs, but the Lions still have so much young talent at their disposal and are primed to challenge again in 2027.

Grade: C-

Carlton
Incoming: Joel Amartey, Lachie Whitfield

Outgoing: Hudson O'Keeffe, Flynn Riley

2026 draft selections: 13, 18, 31, 50, 61, 72, 90

The Blues addressed two areas of weakness this off-season. The addition of free agent Joel Amartey provides spearhead Harry McKay with a stable forward line partner, while the Lachie Whitfield signing offers run, experience, and a kick-first option off halfback, the perfect piece to fit into Josh Fraser's system. Carlton really didn't give up much to land Whitfield, either. And barring Essendon taking a stab at talented father-son prospect Cody Walker with pick No. 1, the club has also ensured it has enough draft capital to match any bids that will come for him.

Grade: A

Collingwood
Incoming: Lachie Neale, Jesse Hogan, Flynn Riley

Outgoing: Scott Pendlebury

2026 draft selections: 11, 30, 67, 68, 70, 88

The Magpies had been crying out for a true inside midfielder, and they landed arguably the best in the competition in Lachie Neale. The two-time Brownlow Medal winner is an elite ball winner and clearance player, and should perfectly complement superstar Nick Daicos. Collingwood also signed Jesse Hogan, a man that won the Coleman Medal just two years ago, and gave up virtually nothing for him. The loss of champion Scott Pendlebury obviously stings, but you have to feel this club is in a stronger position now than it was two weeks ago.

Grade: A

Essendon
Incoming: Jack Bowes, Keidean Coleman

Outgoing: Zach Merrett, Jordan Ridley

2026 draft selections: 1, 17, 25, 80

Former skipper Zach Merrett finally got his wish of a fresh start at the Hawks, while fellow experienced player Jordan Ridley also departs the club for the Cats. The additions of Jack Bowes and Keidean Coleman are fine, but are either going to be difference makers in a side that's been languishing at the bottom of the ladder for several years? I'm not so sure. The only saving grace for the Bombers is that they hold pick No. 1. They simply have to make the most of that selection.

Grade: D

Fremantle
Incoming: Dom Bedendo

Outgoing: Nathan O'Driscoll

2026 draft selections: 19, 40, 60, 63, 78, 96

The Dockers were incredibly quiet during the trade and free agency window, but that's not exactly a bad thing. Remember, if not for Will Ashcroft and Logan Morris, Fremantle win the 2026 premiership. There was absolutely no reason for the Dockers to panic and overpay for someone after their Grand Final heartbreak, instead, this club, with its plethora of youth and talent, should feel as if it can contend for years to come. Trust the process and go again in 2027.

Grade: C

Geelong
Incoming: Toby Greene, Jordan Ridley, Rowan Marshall

Outgoing: Jack Bowes

2026 draft selections: 36, 57, 62, 75, 93

Every year the Cats just find a way to bring big names through the door, and 2026 was no exception. Rowan Marshall was tipped to join 12 months ago and finally makes the move from St Kilda to bolster the club's ruck stocks. Toby Greene adds class, experience, and unrivalled goal-kicking nous to the forward line. Jordan Ridley is a stable and still wildly underrated defensive asset. The best part? To land this trio the club only had to give up midfield depth piece Jack Bowes, and some draft capital. They won't be much of a feature at the upcoming draft, but they don't have to be. These Cats are in win-now mode.

Grade: A

Gold Coast Suns
Incoming: Scott Pendlebury, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler

Outgoing: Ben King

2026 draft selections: 8, 85

Scott Pendlebury might be a champion of the game, but there's no denying the Suns just got worse. The addition of 38-year-old Pendlebury doesn't outweigh the seismic loss of spearhead Ben King, a man who has booted 230 goals over the last four seasons. How do they replace him? Perhaps it's the incoming Aidan Schubert, but he's years away from having a real impact. Making matters worse, it seems Brownlow medallist Matt Rowell is likely to request a trade back to Victoria at the end of next season. This club is in a real precarious spot right now. A penny for Christian Petracca's thoughts...

Grade: C-

GWS Giants
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, Lachie Whitfield

2026 draft selections: 9, 20, 26, 59, 77, 86

Just two years ago Toby Greene, Kieren Briggs, Jesse Hogan, and Lachie Whitfield were probably four of the Giants' most important players. None of them remain at the club after an action-packed trade and free agency window, with GWS instead opting to clear out and trust the youth underneath. It's a move that will either make the Giants look like geniuses or total fools, but even those who are incredibly bullish about the approach would concede there is likely to be some pain on the immediate horizon.

Grade: D

Hawthorn
Incoming: Zach Merrett, Ben King, Josh Goater

Outgoing: Finn Maginness, Aidan Schubert, Sam Butler, Bodie Ryan

2026 draft selections: 29, 37, 71, 94

The Hawks should probably be the 2027 flag favourites after a whirlwind two weeks that's seen them finally land former Essendon skipper Zach Merrett, as well as Ben King. Merrett adds depth, experience, and A-grade ball use to Hawthorn's midfield group, while King provides a focal point in attack, taking the burden off the ageing Jack Gunston. Sure, Hawthorn gave up some depth, but their best 23 has improved out of sight and they still have draft collateral over the next few years to ensure talent keeps coming through the door.

Grade: A+

Melbourne
Incoming: Zane Duursma, Will McLachlan, Bodie Ryan

Outgoing: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

2026 draft selections: 4, 14, 48, 52

Just about everyone panicked when the Demons farewelled premiership heroes Christian Petracca and Clayton Oliver last year, and look how that turned out. This club seems to have a plan for the future and it isn't prepared to compromise on what it wants. Melbourne has nailed its draft picks in recent times and with selections four and 14 this year, you'd expect two more highly talented prospects to join the ranks. Who knows if Zane Duursma will work out, but they've landed him for a fraction of what the Kangaroos gave up at the draft three years ago. It's a low risk punt worth taking.

Grade: C

North Melbourne
Incoming: Nick Blakey

Outgoing: Zane Duursma, Josh Goater

2026 draft selections: 33, 49, 66, 74, 84

Credit to the Kangaroos, they finally landed a big name. The only problem is I'm not sure Nick Blakey is the superstar many are claiming. There's no doubt Blakey will add drive and dash off halfback, but is he the player you look to in the closing stages of a tight game? North also gave up a truckload of future draft capital to get him through the door which will hurt them in the coming years. And then there's the Zane Duursma fiasco. Losing a player the club invested pick No. 4 in just three years ago is an unmitigated disaster. With no selections inside the top 30 this year, it will be a rare draft without the Roos being a major player.

Grade: C+

Port Adelaide
Incoming: Luke Pedlar

Outgoing: Zak Butters

2026 draft selections: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46, 65

You're never going to feel great when a player of Zak Butters' class and calibre walks out the door, but the silver lining for Port Adelaide is that Dougie Cochrane should be set to walk back in. The academy talent is the consensus best player in the upcoming draft and the Power are in a position to match any bids on their man. Expect Port to be heavily involved in the draft over the next couple of years as they look to rebuild around the likes of Cochrane, Connor Rozee, and Jason Horne-Francis.

Grade: B

Richmond
Incoming: Kieren Briggs, Nathan O'Driscoll

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 2, 5, 44, 81

The Tigers found Toby Nankervis' successor in Kieren Briggs, who crosses from the Giants as a free agent. That's a nice win. Nathan O'Driscoll was unable to find a place in Fremantle's best team of late but should receive far more opportunity in the black and yellow jumper in 2027. Richmond has two more picks inside the top five, though they are likely to be shuffled down a few spots with bid matching on Dougie Cochrane and Cody Walker, and they simply must nail them. Even still, this side will remain incredibly young in 2027.

Grade: C

St Kilda
Incoming: Sam Marshall

Outgoing: Rowan Marshall

2026 draft selections: 10, 16, 41, 51, 69, 87

The Saints went all-in last year, signing Tom De Koning, Jack Silvagni, Liam Ryan, and Sam Flanders. They weren't nearly as busy this off-season, and few expected them to be. Long-time ruck Rowan Marshall departs the club for the Cats, while Sam Marshall joins and should bolster their midfield stocks. Outside of that, St Kilda will be hoping to cash in with their two first round draft selections. If not, it could spell the end of Nasiah Wanganeen-Milera's tenure. This team wouldn't want to be starting 2027 slowly...

Grade: C

Sydney Swans
Incoming: N/A

Outgoing: Joel Amartey, Nick Blakey

2026 draft selections: 6, 38, 39, 47, 54, 76, 95

Two best 23 players departed the Swans this past fortnight with halfback Nick Blakey being traded to the Kangaroos and key forward Joel Amartey signing with the Blues as a free agent. Don't forget, Callum Mills is unlikely to suit up for the entire year after suffering an ACL injury during this year's finals campaign. That's three best 23 players to replace! Who knows what's happening with Isaac Heeney and Chad Warner? Swans fans will be praying for a hit with pick No. 6 at the upcoming draft to soften the blow.

Grade: C-

West Coast Eagles
Incoming: Jack Viney, Trent Rivers

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 3, 23, 58, 64, 73, 82

It's clear the Eagles don't want to take the same approach as the Tigers and rely solely on the kids. Instead, they're continuing to add experienced pieces around their young talent in an effort to ease the rebuild and avoid a nosedive in morale. Jack Viney and Trent Rivers add premiership experience to the club and they haven't had to give up too much to get them. West Coast will feature prominently at November's draft with pick No. 3, 23, as well as a compensation pick in the likely scenario that the club's first selection is pushed back by a bid.

Grade: C+

Western Bulldogs
Incoming: Jordon Butts, Finn Maginness, Hudson O'Keeffe, Zak Butters

Outgoing: N/A

2026 draft selections: 42, 53, 55, 83, 89, 91

The Bulldogs now possess the most dynamic midfield trio in the game with Zak Butters joining skipper Marcus Bontempelli and Ed Richards in the red, white, and blue. It's a marquee signing for Luke Beveridge's team that simply has to put them into premiership contention. Jordon Butts also joins the club and will bolster what's traditionally been a weaker defensive unit. Don't forget about key forward star Sam Darcy, who will return from a season-ending ACL injury.

Grade: A+

stories.headline: 'All love': All Blacks inspiring NZ's Rugby League World Cup tilt
stories.summary: Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.
stories.body:
Buoyed by a visit from their All Blacks brothers, Stacey Jones's ambitious Kiwis are out to open the rugby league World Cup with a bang by completing a memorable New Zealand double over Australia.

Five days after the All Blacks crushed the Wallabies 50-19 to clinch the Bledisloe Cup for a 23rd straight year, the Kiwis and Kangaroos clash in a trans-Tasman blockbuster in Sydney on Thursday night to kick off the global showpiece.

Eight ABs, including superstar winger Will Jordan and playmaker Cam Roigard, cast aside the cross-code rivalry to drop into New Zealand's captain's run on Wednesday and throw their support behind Jones's side.

"It's just all love and supporting each other and hopefully we can go watch their game on Saturday too, so it's pretty special," New Zealand captain James Fisher-Harris said.

"How dominant and how they go about their business and represent New Zealand, there's a lot of things that they do that we look up to so yeah, it's pretty cool."

Leading what he believes is "potentially" the best Kiwi forward pack ever, Fisher-Harris says "the plan" is to lift the World Cup and, like the Warriors, continue to inspire a whole new generation of rugby league players back in their homeland just like the 2008 winners did.

"When they won in 2008, I was watching Blairy (Adam Blair) and that, (Nathan) Cayless and obviously Benji (Marshall), so that made me want to go down this path," the enforcer said.

"So hopefully we can do something like that. When you are successful like that, it gets you motivated and you want to play for a certain team or a certain code.

"So that's the plan anyways, to be successful in this World Cup."

Behind the monster pack will be Kayln Ponga for the first time after the talismanic fullback, at 28, opted to represent his parents' homeland.

"He's playing pretty good right about now," Fisher-Harris said of Ponga, who led Newcastle on their magical run from seventh to a 19-18 grand final loss to the Sydney Roosters.

"But it's not just his playing ability, it's his leadership and he's been in the game for a while now.

"He's won a few things but it looks like he's pretty keen to get in that black and white jersey."

Coach Stacey Jones also believes Australia's loss is very much New Zealand's gain.

"For the Knights this year and particularly the back end of the season, he carried them to a grand final," Jones said.

"Obviously had a lot of support around him, but he's got a lot of confidence in his game at the moment and we're just lucky that we've got him on our side."

stories.headline: 15 NFL players, coaches on the hot seat entering Week 6: Quinn, McDaniel, others
stories.summary: What now for Mike McDaniel? Should the Commanders or Eagles consider coaching changes? Could Jacoby Brissett or Brian Thomas Jr. get traded?
stories.body:
Week 6 is about the point where seats start getting hot around the NFL. Five games isn't a huge sample for coaches and players, but it's enough time to see with some confidence that preseason expectations or hopes aren't going to be met. It's enough time for fans to be frustrated and make their feelings known in stadiums and on social media.

Subscribe: 'The Bill Barnwell Show'

There's no joy in seeing anyone around the league lose their job or miss out on an opportunity, but it's also a reality that everybody who works for a team faces on an annual basis. Today, I'm going to run through some of the players and coaches on the proverbial hot seat after the first five weeks of the 2026 NFL season and break down what's going wrong and what might happen next.

In no particular order, I'll hit on three head coaches, two coordinators and 10 players with questions about their futures with their current teams. And I'll begin with a coordinator for a winless team that entered the season with postseason aspirations.

Jump to a player or coach:

McDaniel | Montgomery | Bland | Smack

Bowles | Quinn | Sainristil | Sirianni

Sheppard | Hairston | Jeudy | Brissett

Smith | Thomas | Nix

Mike McDaniel, OC, Los Angeles Chargers
It seems natural to talk about what must be the most disappointing unit in football this season. And it's fair to note that, yet again, injuries have waylaid the Chargers on the offensive side of the ball. In last week's 23-17 loss to the Broncos, the Chargers were down their top two wide receivers (Quentin Johnston and Ladd McConkey, the latter of whom was active but did not play a single snap) and their three best offensive linemen (Joe Alt, Tyler Biadasz and Rashawn Slater). Justin Herbert's lone touchdown pass went to Hayden Rucci, a tight end who was signed off Jacksonville's practice squad in mid-September.

Even so, McDaniel's old employers in San Francisco have had plenty of injuries on offense and things are still humming along just fine for the 49ers. Frankly, even before the injuries really slowed this offense down, things didn't look the way they were supposed to in Los Angeles. The Chargers haven't been able to run the ball all season, ranking 28th in EPA per play on designed rushes.

McDaniel has been insistent on running into heavy boxes with limited success; the Chargers have faced a numbers disadvantage in the run game 36.2% of the time per NFL Next Gen Stats, which is the fifth-worst rate in the league. It's fine to run into loaded boxes if you trust your linemen to pull it off, but the Chargers are averaging 2.5 yards per carry and minus-0.32 EPA per play on those attempts while picking up first downs at the fifth-lowest rate in the NFL.

What has to be more concerning for coach Jim Harbaugh, though, is the regression of Herbert. Through five weeks, Herbert is last among qualifying passers in Total QBR (26.6). By several notable metrics, Herbert has completely collapsed as a passer:

Herbert's sack rate is up, and he leads the league in interceptions with seven. And while a couple of those have been the customary snaps where a Chargers receiver is suddenly allergic to the football at the point of arrival and coughs it up to a defender, Herbert deserves plenty of blame for the problems the Chargers have had as games wear on. He has a 5.0 QBR in the fourth quarter, throwing four picks and taking a league-high five strip sacks. His fourth-down interception against the Broncos last week was one of the worst throws you'll ever see Herbert make, a lowlight he seems adamant about challenging every week once the Chargers get behind late in games.

There's usually not much benefit to making an in-season change at offensive coordinator, given that the positional coaches were likely brought in by that coordinator and would just be running the same scheme if they were promoted to the playcalling role. The most experienced assistant on McDaniel's staff is passing game specialist Adam Gase, which won't inspire much hope among Chargers fans.

They do have Harbaugh, though, and there's a clear line that the offensive coordinator in Los Angeles can't cross. It's one thing to field a disappointing run game or fail to live up to expectations, but the offense can't break Herbert. If McDaniel can't turn things around, and Herbert continues to struggle badly, the Chargers might make a move sooner rather than later.

David Montgomery, RB, Houston Texans
The latest in a series of offseason additions to try to fix a moribund Texans running game, Montgomery hasn't been able to transfer his successful three-year stretch in Detroit to Houston. Though the 2019 third-round pick scored three touchdowns in the Week 1 loss to the Bills, Montgomery has averaged just 2.7 yards per carry and posted a league-worst 23.1% success rate. You can help compensate for those issues with explosive runs, but Montgomery has just one gain of 10-plus yards across 52 carries this season.

Montgomery left last week's win over the Titans in the first half with a groin injury, potentially opening up the door to a larger role for Woody Marks. The second-year pro had what qualifies as a great game on the ground for a Texans back, turning 15 carries into 62 yards while adding four catches for 23 yards as a receiver. The Texans have been hesitant to turn the lead role over to Marks, but Montgomery's struggles and the groin injury might leave them no choice.

DaRon Bland, CB, Dallas Cowboys
Bland was a first-team All-Pro after he picked off nine passes in 2023, but the interceptions have dried up since then. He has just one INT across 24 games since the start of 2024. And when Bland isn't creating significant value with his takeaways, teams find it too easy to pick on him in coverage. He has allowed passer ratings north of 100 in coverage in each of the past three seasons, per Pro-Football-Reference.com, including a career-worst 126.2 mark this season.

Jerry Jones and the Cowboys have had reasons to give Bland a long leash. Despite missing most of the 2024 season with a foot injury, the Cowboys gave their young corner a four-year, $90 million extension before the 2025 season. Bland missed more time last year before pronouncing himself to be all the way back this season ... but he has looked overmatched in coverage. Tez Johnson's 64-yard catch against the Cowboys in primetime last week came on a play where Bland was badly juked and fell to the ground like he was the child in one of those "dad crosses over baby" videos.

The Cowboys didn't really have solutions to replace Bland on the outside at cornerback, but that has changed. Cobie Durant should be set to return from his hamstring injury in the coming weeks, while Joey Porter Jr. will be back in the lineup after missing the loss to the Buccaneers with an illness. When healthy, they should be the starters on the outside for Dallas. Bland could end up in the slot, but the Cowboys have been playing Reddy Steward there, and rookie safety Caleb Downs could move there once Jalen Thompson returns from his hamstring injury.

Dallas restructured Bland's deal just before the season, which reduced his cap hit and made his contract more tradable. But it also creates more dead money if (or more realistically when) the Cowboys decide to move on from the 27-year-old cornerback. Bland is owed $13 million next year, and at the moment, it's only guaranteed for injury. The Cowboys don't want to be on the hook for that money, so it would hardly be a surprise if they took Bland out of the lineup altogether once Durant and Porter are back on the field to avoid triggering those guarantees, which would happen if Bland suffers a significant injury.

Trey Smack, K, Green Bay Packers
Life is tough for rookie kickers. Coaches don't trust you. Fans want an excuse to turn on you. You might get only a handful of kicks to prove that you're an NFL-caliber player. The leash is a little longer if you're a draftee, but competitive teams just don't have much patience with unproven kickers once the season actually begins and games are on the line.

As a sixth-round pick, Smack was clearly prioritized by the Packers as the replacement for Brandon McManus, who might have cost Green Bay its wild-card game with the Bears after missing two field goals and an extra point. And before Sunday, Smack was having a reasonable start to his pro career, having missed just one field goal and one extra point through four games.

In a blowout victory over those same Bears, though, Smack struggled badly. He missed an extra point and field goal attempts from 43 and 47 yards out, matching McManus' performance in the wild-card loss. All three kicks were wide. And though the Packers have to deal with the reality that it's hard to kick in wintry conditions once the calendar hits December and January in Green Bay, this game was played on a 73-degree day with modest wind.

One bad game shouldn't sink Smack. If he struggles in the weeks to come, though, the Packers might not be willing to go into the winter with an inexperienced kicker, especially given what happened to them in the postseason a year ago.

Todd Bowles, HC, Tampa Bay Buccaneers
One win against the Cowboys slowed the criticism of Bowles, whose Bucs had gotten off to an 0-4 start before turning things around against Dallas. The victory ended a stretch where the Buccaneers had gone 2-11 since their bye in 2025, including the first four games of the 2026 season. That run cost them what appeared to be a procession to the NFC South title in 2025 and put them behind the eight ball to start 2026.

With rookie Jalon Daniels in at quarterback for the injured Baker Mayfield, Bowles will have to hope his defense can carry the Bucs in the weeks to come against the likes of the Panthers, Falcons and Bears. Bowles' defense was primarily responsible for the collapse after the bye in 2025, ranking 26th in points allowed per drive and 28th in defensive EPA per snap over that span.

Things have been better on that side of the ball to start the year in 2026. Tampa is fourth in EPA allowed per play and ninth in points allowed per drive. The Buccaneers are somehow doing that with a formula that doesn't make sense. Bowles' defense is blitzing at the fourth-highest rate in the league, but the Bucs rank only 28th in sack rate. Instead, they are winning by stopping the run at the fifth-best rate in the NFL by success rate and getting off the field on third down, where they have the eighth-best defensive stop rate.

Bowles started his second head coaching stint by making three straight playoff appearances, including a blowout victory over the Eagles in 2023. That success bought Bowles some slack. It's also clear that the second-half collapse took a toll on the organization, leading Bowles to fire five assistants after the season. That's usually the last move before a head coach follows his former assistants out the door. If Bowles can stick in the NFC South race and stay afloat until Mayfield returns, he should be back in 2027. If Tampa goes on another losing streak, though, Bowles might have to walk the plank.

Dan Quinn, HC, Washington Commanders
Well, you saw the end of that Giants-Commanders game. While I pin some of the blame for what went wrong on Jayden Daniels and David Blough, as the head coach, Quinn is the one most responsible for making sure his young QB and offensive coordinator know what to do in those situations. Given that Quinn has handed over the defense to Daronte Jones, the 56-year-old should be even more focused on the sort of game management issues that cost the Commanders a shot at a victory Sunday.

Since Quinn stunningly led the Commanders to a 12-5 season and a trip to the NFC Championship Game in his debut year with the organization, things have quickly gone south. Injuries to Daniels sank the team's chances in 2025, but Quinn was blamed for leaving Daniels in the game when he suffered an elbow injury; Washington was trailing by 31 points in the fourth quarter of a loss to the Seahawks.

Washington's defense also collapsed in 2025, finishing 30th in points allowed per drive, leading Quinn to fire defensive coordinator Joe Whitt Jr. The organization invested heavily in free agency to shore up the unit this offseason and hired Jones to take over the defense, but the early results haven't been much better, as the Commanders are up to only 26th in points allowed per possession. They blew a 14-point lead to the Giants on Sunday and couldn't stop Jameis Winston from moving the ball in overtime, with the defense bailed out by a missed field goal and a Cam Skattebo fumble.

Quinn's team is now 3-13-1 over its past 17 games, with one of those victories coming against the Eagles backups in Week 18. Any attempt to draw a line under 2025 as an aberration hasn't been successful, given that the defense has continued to struggle and Daniels has already suffered another elbow injury in 2026. I thought calls to fire Quinn for the endgame on Sunday were too harsh, but there's no denying that this is the sort of disaster that lingers in fans' minds.

If Quinn can't turn things around, there's the risk of this becoming the sort of tenure-defining collapse that Quinn was on the other side of when the Hail Mary past Tyrique Stevenson Sr. in 2024 was the beginning of the end for Matt Eberflus in Chicago.

Mike Sainristil, CB, Washington Commanders
Just as Quinn excelled in 2024 and hasn't seemed like the same difference-maker since then, Sainristil has also struggled to live up to his first year in Washington. A second-round pick who was expected to be a high-end slot cornerback, Sainristil quickly emerged as an option on the outside for the Commanders, finishing ninth in Defensive Rookie of the Year balloting. He then picked off two passes in the postseason, leading to hope that Sainristil could be a young cornerstone for the Commanders.

Instead, he has gone backward. He was one of the many Commanders who struggled last season, allowing a passer rating north of 100 despite intercepting four passes. This year, Sainristil looked even worse in the Week 1 defeat against the Eagles, losing a deep ball in the air to Dontayvion Wicks for Philadelphia's biggest play of the day. He has allowed a 147.6 passer rating in coverage.

Quinn already made his move in Week 3, benching Sainristil after two frustrating starts in favor of veteran journeyman Rasul Douglas. Sainristil ran ahead of Fabian Moreau as the team's nickel cornerback Sunday, playing 48% of the defensive snaps, but the Commanders are about to get 2025 second-round pick Trey Amos back from a fractured fibula. Sainristil will need to play well when he does get on the field to have a shot at winning his job back.

Nick Sirianni, HC, Philadelphia Eagles
Though its impact was muted by its timing in London and the Commanders fiasco that ensued later on Sunday, Sirianni didn't cover himself in glory at the end of Sunday's frustrating loss to the Jaguars. While the Eagles understandably wanted extra yardage to make Jake Elliott's field goal to take the lead easier, Sirianni saw rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon step out of bounds after making a catch, stopping the clock for the Jaguars. And after taking the lead, Sirianni elected to kick the ball into the field of play, with the ensuing return setting the Jags up for a last-second field goal to steal the game away.

Sirianni's decision wasn't quite as cut-and-dried as it might seem. For one, the Eagles might have been just as likely to allow one big completion after a touchback as they were to give up the kickoff return that got Jacksonville in field goal range. If this were one isolated endgame scenario for an otherwise successful organization, the hot seat for Sirianni wouldn't extend outside of Philadelphia sports radio.

Of course, the Eagles have been frustrating for quite a while now. The offense wasn't at its best in 2025, with Philly going 3-4 down the stretch before losing in the wild-card round at home to the 49ers. The Eagles dramatically changed things during the offseason, firing coordinator Kevin Patullo and moving on from legendary offensive line coach Jeff Stoutland. They hired Sean Mannion as the new OC to reimagine the offense by going under center more often and relying on a zone-rushing attack.

Those moves haven't worked. The Eagles are 30th in EPA per play on offense, down from 17th a year ago. Injuries to Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and multiple offensive linemen (and the non-injury-related departures of Cam Jurgens and Lane Johnson) haven't helped, of course, but there really hasn't been a sustained stretch all season where the offense has looked explosive, regardless of who was on the field.

And as I wrote about last year, Sirianni's lack of clear ownership over any one particular piece of the operation makes him more likely to receive blame for what goes wrong than credit for what goes right. Sirianni's résumé through five-plus years as Eagles head coach is as good as anybody's in NFL history, but for various reasons, there's a clear perception that Sirianni isn't the one driving much of that success.

And while Sirianni has racked up a gaudy win-loss record during his time in Philadelphia, the Eagles are 5-7 over their past 12 games, including a three-game losing streak. Three of their next four games are at home against the Panthers, Cowboys and Giants, all games we would expect Sirianni's team to win. If the Eagles win games, even in ugly fashion, fans will tolerate the struggles. But if the losing streak continues, well, the sudden end to Doug Pederson's tenure with the team in 2020 should tell you just how quickly an otherwise successful run can come to a sudden close in Philadelphia.

Kelvin Sheppard, DC, Detroit Lions
When the Lions lost coordinators Ben Johnson and Aaron Glenn after the 2024 season to head coaching gigs, Dan Campbell chose a pair of relatively low-key replacements. He hired John Morton from the Broncos to take over the offense and promoted Sheppard, already on staff as the team's linebackers coach, to run the defense. Given how successful Campbell's prior hires had been, the new coordinators deservedly started their tenure with some credit in the bank.

That credit is all used up. Morton didn't make it through one full year as offensive playcaller. Campbell took over the role during the 2025 season before firing Morton after missing the playoffs. Sheppard made it through Year 1, but unless things improve, it's tough to see him surviving through the end of a second season in the defensive role. The Lions are a disaster on defense, ranking 29th in points allowed per drive and last in EPA per play. They can't get off the field on third down and have allowed teams to convert 81% of their red zone trips into touchdowns, the third-worst figure in the league.

Is that on coaching? I'm skeptical. Watching the Lions closely, I see a defense that simply doesn't have enough talent as opposed to one that makes routine schematic mistakes. The Lions comfortably have the worst secondary in the NFL, a product of injuries (which have cost them one of the league's best safety duos in Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph) and off-field behavior (leading to the release of 2024 first-round pick Terrion Arnold, who admittedly wasn't living up to expectations before being cut amid felony charges of armed robbery and kidnapping).

Longtime starter D.J. Reed hasn't played well, but the players around him shouldn't be expected to make up a solid secondary. Sheppard is running out veterans on low-cost contracts such as Chuck Clark, Roger McCreary, Rock Ya-Sin and Christian Izien as regular defensive backs. Players such as Thomas Harper and Avonte Maddox weren't playing well, either, but they've also gone down injured, leaving the Lions without alternatives. It's telling that Detroit was excited to turn to rookie Keith Abney II, a 5-foot-9 fifth-round pick, as a potential savior at corner against the Cardinals last week. It's difficult to recall a secondary that was less imposing on paper, let alone how it has played in reality.

The good news for the Lions, if there is any, is that the front four is playing better. The Lions have the fifth-best sack rate in the league. They're the second-best tackling team in terms of missed tackle rate, although that doesn't cover situations where the Lions simply aren't close enough to a ball carrier to even attempt a tackle. If the Lions could hold up in coverage, the defense might improve to passable, which would be enough to win plenty of games given the way the offense is playing.

One major reinforcement is on the way in Branch, who has returned to practice and should be back on the field in the next couple of weeks from his Achilles injury. Abney had a solid start against the Cardinals and should feature in the defense more often moving forward. And though Joseph's future is unclear after suffering a knee injury last year, the hope is that the Lions will have the 2024 first-team All-Pro back at some point in 2026.

If Abney and Branch can't right the ship, something will need to change. General manager Brad Holmes is aggressive and could look to make a move at the trade deadline, with Campbell admitting that the Lions were in on the Joey Porter Jr. negotiations before the Cowboys swooped in and traded for the Steelers corner. Sheppard will obviously hope to get more help, but the Lions can't compete for a title if their defense continues to blow leads in the fourth quarter.

Maxwell Hairston, CB, Buffalo Bills
The reckoning might have already come for Hairston, Buffalo's first-round pick in the 2025 draft. His rookie year was compromised by a knee injury that cost him the first six games of the campaign. He ended up starting just three games all season and then missed the two postseason games that ended Sean McDermott's tenure with an ankle injury.

This season was supposed to be a fresh start for Hairston, but his first month was a mess. The 23-year-old allowed two touchdown passes in the 29-26 loss to the Patriots, leading defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard to publicly encourage Hairston to temper his emotions. Hairston also left the locker room after the defeat without speaking to the media before returning and apologizing a day later.

The Bills have said the right thing publicly, but actions speak louder than words. Against the Rams on Monday, Hairston's snap share cratered with the return of Christian Benford. The Bills kept Davison Igbinosun in the lineup ahead of Hairston, who played just 15 snaps on defense. Igbinosun committed a pass interference penalty in the red zone and allowed a touchdown catch, which won't help his case, but he still appears to be ahead of Hairston on the depth chart.

Jerry Jeudy, WR, Cleveland Browns
The Browns are excited about their young wide receiver duo of Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion, although Concepcion was forced out of last week's loss to the Jets with a concussion. Harold Fannin Jr. is a building block at tight end, too. There's less chatter about Jeudy, whose role in the offense has been inconsistent. Jeudy saw steady snaps last week after Concepcion's injury, but he had been playing about half of the offensive snaps on a weekly basis beforehand, dropping down to 38% in the Week 4 win over the Steelers.

Jeudy has a line of eight catches for 81 yards this season, but he's still only 27 years old and two years removed from a 1,229-yard campaign for the Browns in 2024. It's tough to see a long-term future for him in Cleveland, but how he plays over the next few weeks might determine whether there's real interest at the trade deadline from a team that wants to give the 2020 first-round pick a meaningful role. If not, Jeudy might lose snaps to Boston, Concepcion, Isaiah Bond and tight ends in the second half of the year.

Jacoby Brissett, QB, Arizona Cardinals
I have been an avowed Brissett fan for years given his incredibly low interception rate and ability to at least competently sustain just about any offense in football. Through five games in 2026, though, Brissett is averaging just 5.6 yards per attempt and has thrown five picks. One of those was a Hail Mary against the Lions last week, but Brissett threw three interceptions in the previous week's loss to the Giants, including a pick-six on the final snap of the game to Deonte Banks.

Brissett's ability to pick up first downs on sneaks and complete a high percentage of his passes appeals to Total QBR, which has him 16th among all quarterbacks through five games. But with Brissett 30th in yards per dropback and the Cardinals last by a considerable margin in explosive play rate (5.5%) on offense, this is a case where I think my own feelings and those of the organization might disagree with QBR.

The Cardinals aren't particularly motivated to win games this season given the likelihood that they'll draft a quarterback in 2026. They're also likely interested in seeing what they have in third-round pick Carson Beck, who posted a 125.4 passer rating in the preseason. If there's a trade market for Brissett at the deadline, the Cardinals might consider just moving forward with Beck and Gardner Minshew II as their two options under center. And if not, Brissett might be sitting behind the rookie by the time we get to November anyway.

Genesis Smith, S, Los Angeles Chargers
It's tough to be a rookie on a collapsing team that's drastically coming up short of expectations, and Smith isn't the biggest problem in Los Angeles. And the fourth-round pick did come up with two interceptions of Josh Allen in Week 3. But Smith has otherwise struggled in coverage, having a particularly rough day against the Raiders in Week 2. He also appeared to be at fault on the lone touchdown pass of the day for the Broncos on Sunday, flying into the flat to take a covered receiver while letting Courtland Sutton run past him for an easy score.

The Chargers haven't had star safety Derwin James Jr. on the field for the past couple of games, but the five-time Pro Bowler should be back in the lineup after recovering from a hamstring injury. Jim Harbaugh could choose to treat the rest of the year as a lost cause and stick with his young guys to get them reps, but I wouldn't be shocked if the Chargers tried to get their most reliable players on the field and stuck with veterans James, Tony Jefferson and Elijah Molden as their three safeties when they're all healthy.

Brian Thomas Jr., WR, Jacksonville Jaguars
Though the Jaguars keep winning, Thomas' role in the offense continues to shrink. After a disappointing 2025 season was chalked up to an ankle issue that made it painful for him to run, hopes were high that he would be able to get back to his rookie-year level of production in a second season under Liam Coen in 2026.

So far, Thomas has nine catches for 105 yards through five games, including a doughnut in Sunday's win over the Eagles. (He did nearly catch a touchdown, only to narrowly step out of bounds.) The coaching staff also doesn't seem particularly desperate to get the 2024 first-round pick on the field, with Thomas playing just 48.2% of the offensive snaps. In recent weeks, the Jaguars have preferred rookie sixth-round pick Josh Cameron to Thomas for his blocking and big-play ability, particularly when they get into larger personnel groupings.

The Jaguars are committed to Parker Washington and Jakobi Meyers as their top two wideouts and want to play with Brenton Strange and Nate Boerkircher on the field, which leaves a limited role for Thomas. Trading Thomas would also open up more opportunities for Travis Hunter, who has played just 21 offensive snaps while starring on defense. The organization has repeatedly insisted that it has no interest in trading Thomas, but at some point, having a valuable young player wasting away on your bench can't be the best thing for the player or the team.

Bo Nix, QB, Denver Broncos
Let's frame this one appropriately and be clear. I don't think the Broncos are about to bench Nix for backup Jarrett Stidham, who hasn't been particularly impressive as a pro and didn't play well in last season's AFC title game loss to the Patriots while filling in for the injured starter. The hot seat here is more in the big picture, with Nix becoming eligible for a contract extension after the season and a decision on his fifth-year option in 2028 (at a projected $29.9 million) coming due next spring.

Whether it has been a product of Nix recovering from the ankle injury that ended his 2025 season, not feeling right in Davis Webb's version of the offense or simply being too antsy about where to go with the football, he hasn't been an effective quarterback through five games in 2026. Nix's 41.5 Total QBR is 24th in the league. He's averaging just 5.8 yards per attempt, and only 27.8% of his throws are producing first downs, the fourth-worst rate in the league.

In years past, Nix has produced a relatively high floor by avoiding mistakes and creating plays with his legs, generating first downs for an offense that wasn't getting them through the air. Nix's interception rate and sack rate are still much better than league average, but he's generating just 7 rushing yards and 1.2 first downs per game as a runner, down from 23 rush yards and two first downs per game over the prior two seasons.

Throughout his career, Nix has been an erratic quarterback given his propensity to throw off-platform and on the move. He has a strong arm, but getting the most out of that arm requires Nix to set his feet and throw with a solid base, and all of his movement makes it difficult to actually access his arm strength. When he's playing well, Nix is an accurate passer. When he's not, the ball is all over the place, and Nix can struggle with just getting the ball out before routes have even developed.

Expectations for the offense were high after Nix's performance in the divisional round win over the Bills and the offseason acquisition of Jaylen Waddle, who gave the Broncos a much-needed threat at all three levels across from Courtland Sutton. As the Broncos struggled through the first month of the season, frustration for Denver's slow start on offense naturally fell on Webb, the 31-year-old former quarterback who had taken over playcalling duties from Sean Payton to start the season.

It wasn't much of a surprise when Payton reclaimed playcalling responsibilities before last Sunday's game over the Chargers. Yet Nix might have looked worse in Payton's first game back at the helm against what has been one of the league's most unimposing defenses. Nix went 16-of-27 for just 123 yards, and the Broncos converted only one third down in 12 tries. All 20 of their points came on drives that started on Los Angeles' side of the field.

The Broncos have more insight into the status of Nix's ankle than we do, and it's possible that the 26-year-old is playing through pain. Even if we take a step back and look at his full career, though, Nix is 19th in Total QBR since entering the league. He's 22nd in yards per dropback and 29th in yards per attempt and first-down rate. And Nix has done that with one of the league's best offensive lines and an elite architect designing the offense and calling plays.

The Broncos were hoping Nix would take a step forward after his great performance in the postseason and the addition of Waddle. If Nix doesn't get there, will the Broncos want to commit to him as their quarterback of the future on a second contract?

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Martínez's future at Man United in doubt after bust-up
stories.summary: Lisandro Martínez's future at Manchester United is in question after he pointed fingers at the club's board. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Lisandro Martínez's future at Manchester United is in question after his scathing critique of the club's board, while Bayern Munich could offer Florian Wirtz an escape route from the Premier League should he want to end his stay at Liverpool.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- The future of Manchester United center back Lisandro Martínez has been called into question after his public criticism of the club's bosses, reports Sky Sports. The 28-year-old's contract expires in the summer, and there are real doubts about whether it will be renewed, especially as the Red Devils aim to revamp their defence as they look at new center backs and left backs. Martinez pushed for a move to Atlético Madrid in the summer, but no suitable offer came in for United to consider.

- Bayern Munich are keeping close tabs on the situation of Liverpool attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz, according to TEAMtalk. The 23-year-old hasn't reached the levels expected since making his move from Bayer Leverkusen to Anfield last summer, and there is a belief within the Allianz Arena that the Germany international would be open to a Bundesliga return. While the discussions within the German club are growing, they still remain exploratory rather than official.

- AS Monaco's Folarin Balogun and Atletico Madrid's Alexander Sørloth are the main names being looked at as Juventus aim to sign a striker, as reported by Tuttosport. Luciano Spalletti likes both strikers, and Balogun in particular is likely to make a transfer in January, as the 25-year-old's proposed summer move to Everton fell through due to a scandal involving his medical, and he has been left out of Monaco's Conference League squad. Jonathan David's loan from Juventus to Atleti could help open the door for Sorloth to go the other way.

- Liverpool have stepped up their pursuit of Tijuana attacking midfielder Gilberto Mora, according to TEAMtalk. Mora turned 18 years old yesterday, which removes any FIFA barrier to the Mexico international moving abroad and means a transfer could be possible in January. The Reds have followed up their earlier enquiries and are now strong contenders to sign Mora, who Tijuana want £30 million for, which would be a Liga MX record. Arsenal are also serious contenders, Borussia Dortmund and Benfica have previously held talks with Mora's representatives, while Real Madrid, Barcelona, Manchester City, Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain are also admirers.

stories.headline: Brewers stun Dodgers with back-to-back homers in 7th inning and take 3-0 lead in NLCS with 6-2 win
stories.summary: — Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell to regain the lead in the seventh inning, and the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — Jake Bauers and Garrett Mitchell hit back-to-back homers off Blake Snell to regain the lead in the seventh inning, and the Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 6-2 on Wednesday to take a 3-0 lead in the National League Championship Series.


The Dodgers had just taken a 2-1 lead in the bottom of the sixth before getting stunned. The loss pushed the two-time defending World Series champions to the brink of elimination. They had only trailed 3-0 in a best-of-seven postseason series once previously in franchise history, getting swept by the Baltimore Orioles in the 1966 World Series.


Game 4 is Thursday at Dodger Stadium.


Coming into the seventh, Snell had retired 14 in a row. The first pitch of the game thrown by the two-time Cy Young Award winner was a home run by Jackson Chourio, and his last pitch was Mitchell's solo shot.


Andrew Vaughn drew a seven-pitch walk to open the inning and was replaced by pinch-runner Christian Yelich. Bauers followed with a 412-foot shot to right field on the 11th pitch of the at-bat for a 3-2 lead as most of Milwaukee's dugout came onto the field to celebrate. Mitchell was next and his drive traveled 428 feet to right-center, chasing Snell.


Snell gave up four runs and four hits in six innings, struck out nine and walked two.


The Brewers are on the verge of sweeping the Dodgers in what would be a reversal of last year's NLCS, when the Dodgers eliminated Milwaukee in four games. The Brewers have never beaten the Dodgers in three previous postseason series.


The Brewers extended the lead to 5-2 on Justin Wrobleski's wild pitch that scored Brice Turang, who reached on an infield single to third and moved up on William Contreras' single in the eighth. They added another run on Joey Ortiz's two-strike RBI single in the ninth.


The offensively starved Dodgers took their first lead, 2-1, on Will Smith's two-run double off reliever Abner Uribe in the sixth.


Uribe followed rookie starter Robert Gasser and he loaded the bases on walks to Teoscar Hernández, Kyle Tucker and Shohei Ohtani. Smith, who came in hitting .043, doubled to left-center for his first hit of the NLCS.


DL Hall took over from Uribe, allowing one hit and striking out two before turning it over to Trevor Megill in the eighth.


The Dodgers played from behind again after Snell's leadoff homer to Chourio as fans were still heading to their seats.


After that, Mitchell walked and Cooper Pratt singled in the second before Snell retired 14 in a row — six on strikeouts — before getting hammered in the seventh.


The Dodgers had runners on base in all but three innings, but couldn't get enough across. They have yet to homer in the NLCS.


Ohtani was 1 for 2 with a walk hitting sixth in the order, the lowest he's batted since joining the Dodgers three years ago.

stories.headline: When can Kimi Antonelli win the F1 title? Earliest date, points needed and remaining races
stories.summary: Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli took another big step towards his first world title after outscoring his two closest championship rivals, George Russell and Lewis Hamilton, at the Singapore Grand Prix.

The 20-year-old, who has the potential to set a new record for the youngest Formula 1 champion this year, now leads Mercedes teammate Russell by 102 points in the standings with a maximum of 150 points still up for grabs.

The substantial lead means he could be crowned champion as early as Oct. 24 at the U.S. Grand Prix in Austin, but the maths around that calculation are slightly complicated by question marks over the final two races of the season. The grands prix in Qatar and Abu Dhabi are currently scheduled to go ahead on Nov. 29 and Dec. 6, but escalations in the war between the United States and Iran have the potential to force the cancellation of both rounds.

F1 has put a contingency plan in place to hold a single round at Imola if Qatar and Abu Dhabi are cancelled, but doing so would cut the championship short by one round and mean only 125 points are available to any single driver before the end of the year. Such a scenario would change the maths around the championship fight, making it easier for Antonelli to be crowned champion in Austin.

- 'Chucky' Verstappen is back. Luckily for Antonelli and Mercedes, it's too late

- Max Verstappen takes back-to-back wins with dominant drive at Singapore GP

- Lewis Hamilton calls Singapore GP strategy 'painful lesson' after Ferrari apology

Alongside Russell and Hamilton, Max Verstappen, Charles Leclerc and Lando Norris are still mathematically in contention for this year's championship, although the incredibly slim hopes of Leclerc and Norris would be snuffed out entirely by the cancellation of the races in the Middle East.

What does Antonelli need to do to be crowned champion in Austin?
Assuming the final two races go ahead as planned, Antonelli's chances of clinching the title in Austin remain relatively slim. The Mercedes driver would need to win in Texas, with his teammate Russell finishing ninth or lower and Hamilton finishing fifth or lower.

Such a scenario would put Antonelli 125 points ahead of Russell with 125 points remaining, but even if Antonelli failed to score another point and Russell won all the remaining rounds after Austin, Antonelli would still be crowned champion on countback of race victories (by that stage Antonelli would be on nine and Russell on three with five races remaining).

If the championship is shortened by the season ending in Imola rather than Abu Dhabi, Antonelli would only need to leave Austin with a lead of 100 points over his rivals.

Such a scenario would result in the following permutations:

If Antonelli wins in Austin he would be crowned champion regardless of where the others finish.
If Antonelli finishes second, he would be crowned champion if Russell doesn't win the race.
If Antonelli finishes third, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes off the podium.
If Antonelli finishes fourth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes behind him and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes fifth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fourth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes sixth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes fifth or lower and Hamilton does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes seventh, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes sixth or lower and Hamilton does not finish in the top two.
If Antonelli finishes eighth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes seventh or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top two and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes ninth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes eighth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli finishes tenth, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton does not finish in the top three and Verstappen does not win the race.
If Antonelli fails to score, he would be crowned champion if Russell finishes ninth or lower, Hamilton finishes fifth or lower and Verstappen does not win the race.

What's the minimum Antonelli needs to do be crowned champion?
Another way to look at the championship is the minimum amount of points Antonelli needs to score over the remaining rounds to secure the title regardless of what other drivers achieve. Assuming Qatar and Abu Dhabi go ahead, he needs 49 points over the remaining rounds, which could be achieved with as little as five sixth place finishes and one fifth place finish over the rest of the season.

If only five races remain, Antonelli would need just 24 points to secure the title, which would be attainable with two seventh place finishes and three eighth place finishes at the remaining rounds.

stories.headline: Man City's Antoine Semenyo on missed chances against PSG: 'Beating myself up'
stories.summary: Antoine Semenyo expressed his frustration over his missed chances in Manchester City's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.
stories.body:
Antoine Semenyo expressed his frustration over his missed chances in Manchester City's defeat to Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League on Wednesday.

The European champions raced into a 3-0 lead in just over 30 minutes at the Etihad to stun the hosts before an improved second-half showing led by Erling Haaland saw the game eventually end 4-2 to PSG.

City pushed PSG hard for a way back, racking up 27 shots and a xG of 2.5. However, their finishing was wayward, with Semenyo especially wasteful. He had an xG of 0.45 and missed a gilt-edged chance soon after Haaland's first goal that would have made the score 3-2.

"It's quite frustrating, to be honest. I think I'm beating myself up a little bit at the moment from all the chances that I missed," Semenyo said in a post-match interview to CBS.

"But I think collectively it was just the reaction and we did so well, caused so many problems. So just unfortunate not to score. So we just take the positives and go again."

PSG's credentials as Europe's best team were again underlined in a scintillating attacking performance at the Etihad, and they look well placed to win a third-successive Champions League title.

They condemned City to their first defeat of the season in all competitions and could have put five goals past them had it not been for Ferran Torres' penalty-miss towards the end.

- Man City can't compete with PSG, the Champions League's gold standard

- Halftime lead worried Luis Enrique in game PSG 'could have lost' to City

"They're one of the best obviously ... Ballon d'Or candidates all around in their team," Semenyo said.

"They made it very hard for us today. We knew what to expect, very unorthodox, credit to them. That's why they're back-to-back European champions."

stories.headline: Dream's Gray has minor procedure on hand ahead of Finals opener
stories.summary: Allisha Gray, who has missed the Dream's past two playoff games because of a left hand injury, is still day-to-day heading into the WNBA Finals after undergoing a minor procedure.
stories.body:
Four-time All-Star Allisha Gray underwent a minor procedure on her left hand and is still considered day-to-day for the Atlanta Dream heading into the WNBA Finals, she said Tuesday.

"Progress is great," Gray told WSB-TV when asked at practice whether she'd play in Game 1. "As of right now just day-to-day, and you'll see."

Gray did not clarify whether she had surgery on her hand, and the team declined to say when the procedure occurred.

She was seen taking shots at practice Tuesday, a day before the team travels to the Bay Area for Saturday's Finals opener against No. 2 seed Golden State.

Gray, the top scorer for the No. 4 seed Dream, has missed the past two playoff games after injuring the hand in the first half of Game 1 in a semifinal series against the New York Liberty. She was listed as questionable heading into Game 3 last Friday against New York and went through warmups before being ruled out "in the interest of caution," according to coach Karl Smesko.

The Dream advanced to the Finals with a three-game sweep.

Gray, a 6-foot guard out of South Carolina, averaged 19.0 points, 3.5 rebounds, 2.6 assists and 1.4 steals this year while appearing in all 44 regular-season games. She was also the Dream's top scorer (22.0 points per game) during their first-round sweep of the No. 5 seed Washington Mystics.

The Dream and Valkyries will both be competing for their first WNBA championship.

stories.headline: Spurs debut three-guard lineup of Fox, Harper, Castle in preseason win
stories.summary: Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed the three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Suns on Wednesday.
stories.body:
SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs coach Mitch Johnson finally deployed a three-guard lineup featuring De'Aaron Fox, Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle in a 123-103 preseason win over the Phoenix Suns on Wednesday, explaining "it's time to push forward appropriately" the team's "natural evolution that will still take time."

That was apparent in the group's choppy start as Harper and Castle combined to miss their first five shots before Fox, making his preseason debut, subbed out with 6:57 left in the opening quarter.

But by the time the buzzer sounded for intermission, Fox, Harper and Castle had combined for 31 points, 12 rebounds and six assists in helping San Antonio seize a 60-49 halftime lead.

"I'm glad they got to play some together and we got some reps out there," Johnson said. "I thought we started the game with some very sloppy possessions, and everybody will have to have a better start to games and a better approach with that."

Fox drilled a corner 3-pointer with one second left for the Spurs' final points of the first half. Castle led all scorers with a game-high 18 points, including 14 from the free throw line. Harper, who finished with nine points, drew the most raucous cheers from the Frost Bank Center crowd with 34.5 seconds left in the second quarter, when he caught a Devin Vassell miss for a rim-rocking tip dunk.

Fox even slammed home a poster dunk in the first half.

"I felt like we were trying to do the right things at the beginning, but we scored so few points," Spurs forward Victor Wembanyama said. "When it clicked, it clicked. The biggest thing is I've got handlers all around me, guys that we want to put the ball in their hands and pick and roll around me. That makes things easier."

Fox, Harper and Castle spent a total of 11 minutes on the court together in the opening half, combining for 19 points to finish with a net rating of plus-10. Fox, Harper and Castle played only 69 minutes together all of last season, including 25 in the NBA Finals, and opponents outscored the Spurs by 47 points in those minutes.

By comparison, the Spurs finished with a plus-9.4 net rating when Fox and Castle shared the court in the regular season, plus-6.2 with Fox and Harper, and plus-11.0 with Harper and Castle.

Fox said the guards spoke over the summer in France, when they visited Wembanyama, about the prospect of potentially playing in the starting lineup together.

"Obviously, when we were in the Finals, and just throughout the playoffs, there were times where we all three played together, a lot more than we did throughout the regular season," Fox said. "But we knew there was a chance that we'd all be starting or at least sharing the court together. We're all excited for it."

Johnson initially announced ahead of last week's exhibition opener against the Atlanta Hawks that Fox, Harper and Castle would join Wembanyama and Vassell in the starting lineup. But approximately 20 minutes after that announcement, Fox arrived at Frost Bank Center experiencing general soreness, which caused San Antonio's strength and conditioning staff to hold out the veteran guard.

Fox played only the first half against the Suns, spending 18 minutes, 33 seconds on the court.

Johnson, meanwhile, explained the logic behind playing Fox, Harper and Castle in the starting lineup.

"I understand the narrative around it. I always land on the same reasoning at the very end of it," he said. "They're three of our better players. I know the majority of their lives, maybe their highlight tape is typically with the basketball in their hands. But De'Aaron Fox has played with other handlers and played off the ball a ton. Steph Castle won a national championship [at UConn], basically not touching the ball ever for the start of a possession. They've done it here. We didn't do it a lot last year.

"Dylan was a rookie who couldn't play more than 20 minutes for half the season [in 2025-26] because he was going to cough up a lung because he wasn't in shape. I think they can dribble, pass, shoot, defend, make winning plays. They're unselfish. They have good size."

ESPN Research contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Ferreira, De Sousa Brito help Dallas end Sounders' unbeaten run with 1-0 victory
stories.summary: Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half to give FC Dallas a 1-0 victory over Seattle Sounders on Wednesday night.
stories.body:
FRISCO, Texas -- Kaick Ferreira scored in the second half and Daniel De Sousa Britto made it stand up as FC Dallas beat Seattle 1-0 on Wednesday night, ending the Sounders' four-match win streak and an unbeaten run that reached nine.

Ferreira took a pass from defender Osaze Urhoghide in the 63rd minute and scored for the fourth time this season after scoring twice in 27 appearances as a 19-year-old rookie last year. Urhoghide's helper was his third after collecting one last season in 27 matches as a rookie.

De Sousa Britto finished with seven saves for his third clean sheet in six starts with Dallas (14-7-8). He had 14 shutouts in 78 career starts with the San Jose Earthquakes before joining the club.

Andrew Thomas totaled two saves for Seattle (11-10-8), which went 4-0-5 during its unbeaten streak.

Seattle beat Dallas 2-1 at home to close out April.

Dallas improves to 7-2-5 at home, while the Sounders drop to 4-6-5 on the road.

stories.headline: 'I'm a competitor': Cody Walker primed and ready for the next step
stories.summary: Cody Walker has lived a year of Carlton's ups and downs before having even been drafted. He's learned a lot about the business of footy and what he needs to do to take the next step, as his own AFL career begins.
stories.body:
Cody Walker had a front row seat to Carlton's tumultuous season. In line meetings, at team dinners, out of the Michael Voss era and into the Josh Fraser fairytale. From door stops to crisis meetings, it was an eye opening introduction to the big business of footy for the son-of-a-gun.

"I actually reflect on it a bit now and consider how low a club can get. Being on the inside with all the outside noise that we had when all the Vossy stuff was going down, it was really quite interesting to see," Walker tells ESPN.

"Then going from that to top of the AFL and beating Brisbane and Fremantle towards the end of the season, seeing how good a club can feel and get. For that to both happen in one season I find it quite interesting. I'm sort of glad it happened in a way that I get to experience both worlds."

In the midst of their early season malaise, Blues players were subjected to abuse walking off the ground after second half fadeouts and even rocked up to Ikon Park with anti-Voss graffiti on the club walls. That included Walker as he trained full-time with the squad.

"All the outside noise tears you apart a little bit. To see fans out the front of Ikon Park sort of giving it to you, and open training to have people yelling out at you and it's your fans, they've got Carlton stuff on, but they're yelling out to you, it's pretty full on."

From 1-8 under Voss, the Blues stormed home under Fraser, winning their next six starts and claiming a remarkable win in a wildcard final against Melbourne.

A fractured playing group was united under a first-time head coach and Walker was along for the ride.

"It was quite an eye opener how sad it can get inside a club. You sort of have to keep to yourself in those moments and just get around the boys," he says.

"We definitely had to stick together as a group, and Fraser's been really good at that. We did a lot together this year, the players grabbed me along to every dinner they had. It was so good, such a good experience."

That finals finish means Carlton receives no discount on matching a bid on the son of high-flyer Andrew, with the pair likely to become the first father-son duo to each be selected in the top five of an AFL Draft.

Walker's talent deserves to see him taken at pick 2, just like his dad.

An electric midfielder blessed with the twitchiness, agility and burst to free himself from stoppages, Walker enjoyed a brilliant campaign with Carlton's VFL side and cemented his status in the 2026 draft.

There's no doubting his mercurial talent and its fit alongside Patrick Cripps, Sam Walsh, and Jagga Smith, but Walker isn't yet the complete package, and he's the first one to acknowledge it.

"I think my burst out of stoppage and ball-winning is my 'one wood'... when I look back on footage and see for myself how dangerous I can look going out of stoppage, it's really eye-opening for me," he tells ESPN.

"My improvements I want going into next year, I want to improve every part of my fundamentals. I've got a little bit of disposal efficiency which can let me down, but I'll put a power of work into kicking and handballing.

"It got to the point where I was doing two or three sessions a week, and that includes Diesel Williams helping me out.

"I've got so many good people around me and I can already feel that I'm getting better at those things. I'm pretty straightforward in what I want to get better at and I like getting harsh feedback from coaches that I can work on.

"No one's really pissing in my pocket about something I need to work on and I don't realise it until I'm maybe on [the MCG] one day and it's a problem for me if I'm missing kicks or missing handballs."

Walker's final game before he turns professional wasn't in Carlton's VFL side, at the national championships with Vic Country or back with the Bendigo Pioneers. It was in the Goulburn Valley Football League playing for hometown Echuca, and he spent most of his lead-up convincing the Blues' General Manager of Football to let him go.

"I actually sat down with Chris Davies about two weeks before the granny. I was like, 'What are the chances I get to play?'" Walker recalls to ESPN.

"He was like, 'Mate, we're not going to stop you. Preferably, I think it's the wrong decision, but it's all your choice.'"

Walker was determined to enjoy one more stint out in the country with his best mates after a massive top-age season, but injured his ankle during training the week after that conversation with Davies. It ruled him out of the qualifying final, but he still had an eye towards their qualification into the big dance.

"I went home for two weeks and I was training with Echuca and I just got addicted. I called up the club and a few people there and I was like 'I think I'm going to play, I'm doing it'. I'm so glad I did it."

Walker had 20 disposals, eight score involvements, and kicked a goal off the wing in Echuca's 13-goal win over the Shepparton Swans.

It underlined the values that have made Walker rise and rise through junior football ranks. His competitive spirit and genuine love of footy through rich bloodlines continually stands out. Carlton supporters have known of Walker's footballing exploits for years, but they may not know what makes him tick.

That attitude was on show in the 2km time trial at the AFL Draft combine. Walker led his group of runners by the length of the straight, finishing nine seconds ahead of second place. It's his inner motivation that drives him to compete against the best, and oftentimes that means competing against himself.

It's why he has a grin on his face when asked why he even ran despite some Blues supporters bemoaning his name rising higher on rival clubs' draft boards.

"It was probably to beat my [personal best]... my PB was 6:13, I was feeling good and I had a bit in the tank," he says.

"Personally I'm a competitor. I do want to see where I'm at as of right now compared to maybe three months later when I do a 2k at the club."

Walker smashed that time, finishing in 6:04 minutes and on the podium despite running in a slower pack.

It's given Carlton more to consider, lacking the points to match a bid at pick 1 but desperate to secure its second elite father-son prospect in as many years after Harry Dean was taken with pick two in 2025.

"I've got plenty of trust in the club with what they can do in my scenario," Walker says.

"I love the Carlton Football Club and I'm really thankful they've given me this year and it would be a really cool thing to end up at my dad's club. There's a lot of history there."

stories.headline: NRL: Spencer Leniu signs with Eels after early Roosters release
stories.summary: Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Spencer Leniu has signed a four-year deal with Parramatta just days after winning his fourth NRL premiership with the Sydney Roosters.

Leniu finished his three-year stint at the Tricolours on a high after a stellar performance in their 19-18 win over Newcastle to secure the 2026 trophy.

The NSW Origin representative added the Roosters' premiership ring to the three he won with Penrith from 2021-2023.

Leniu was granted a release from the final year of his Roosters contract, which will give the club some salary cap reprieve

The hard-hitting forward's Eels contract is reportedly worth more than the $850,000 per year he was making with Easts, where he spent much of his time coming off the bench.

He is expected to play a more active role in blue and gold, leading the line for the Eels' forward pack.

The westward move will see the former Panther reunite with good friend Jarome Luai, but first the pair will both suit up for Toa Samoa at the Rugby League World Cup.

Eels general manager of football Mark O'Neill shared his delight at signing one of the game's "premier enforcers".

"We're thrilled to have Spencer join the Parramatta Eels and become part of what we're building at this club," O'Neill said in a statement.

"He's one of the elite middle forwards in the game and has consistently performed on the biggest stages throughout his career.

The exit of Leniu adds to the exodus of stars from the Roosters premiership lineup.

Angus Crichton and Mark Nawaqanitawase are rugby-bound, Daly Cherry-Evans is joining Hull FC, while Daniel Tupou retired this week after his 307-game career.

Connor Watson, who missed the title decider due to concussion, has signed for a season with St George Illawarra Dragons.

Roosters coach Trent Robinson said Leniu had been a strong contributor during his time at the club.

"Spencer has brought a lot to our group over the last three years, both through the way he plays and the energy and personality he brings every day," Robinson said in a statement on Thursday.

"He brings an intensity and competitiveness to everything he does, and he challenges the people around him to be better.

"To see him finish his time here as a premiership winner is something he should be really proud of, and something we'll always share together."

With his departure announced at the Roosters' awards night on Wednesday, Leniu said he would leave the club on a high.

""I'm proud to have worn the Roosters jersey and I'll always have a lot of love and respect for the club, the boys and everyone who has supported me during my time here," said Leniu.

"Winning a premiership with this group and sharing that with the boys, our families and everyone at the club is something I'll carry with me for the rest of my life."
